title: Erasure law for the vector reader
statement: For any type $A$, any field reader that maps a bit string to either failure or a value in $A$ together with a remaining suffix, any length $n$, and any bit string $x$, discarding the vector parsed by the length-$n$ reader gives the same result as applying $n$ times the skipper that discards each field's value and retains its suffix.
hypotheses_covered: $r$ is a field reader from bit strings to optional values in $A$ paired with suffixes
replaced:
For every field reader with values in a type $A$, every length $n$, and every
bit string $x$: discarding the parsed vector from the length-$n$ vector reader
equals iterating the value-discarding version of the field reader $n$ times.
